papers.title: A 3+1 formalism for self-similar expanding grids in computational relativistic and Newtonian magnetohydrodynamics
papers.abstract: Astrophysical systems frequently undergo spatial expansion during their evolution. Simulating these systems with standard conservative codes for hydrodynamics and magnetohydrodynamics using fixed grids is challenging, particularly when attempting to preserve high resolution across vast changes in physical scale. While moving or expanding meshes, or adapting mesh refinement, can address this issue, they introduce computational complexity and are notoriously difficult to implement robustly. We aim to overcome these barriers by providing an easily implementable strategy that empowers the community to achieve high-fidelity results and establishes expanding-grid approaches as a highly accessible standard practice. Leveraging the gauge freedom of the 3+1 formalism for MHD on curved manifolds, a foundation common to all general relativistic fluid dynamics codes, we demonstrate how an expanding coordinate system can be implemented purely through a simple modification of the underlying metric. This requires zero modifications to the numerical mesh or the core structure of the code, and the necessary addition or modification of metric terms can be easily accomplished even in Newtonian MHD. We apply this framework to standard test problems in both relativistic and Newtonian hydrodynamics and MHD, directly comparing the results of fixed and expanding coordinates. Our tests demonstrate the full consistency, accuracy, and robustness of this metric-based expansion approach, as the original conservative formulations is fully preserved. Through a simple coordinate transformation and a re-definition of the metric tensor, any general relativistic MHD code can be effortlessly transformed into an expanding-grid code. This approach elegantly guarantees both fundamental conservation properties and the solenoidal condition for the magnetic field, and can be readily extended to include non-ideal effects.

papers.title: Particle Identification Studies using a Highly Granular Crystal Electromagnetic Calorimeter
papers.abstract: A proposal for the Circular Electron Positron Collider electromagnetic calorimeter is a highly granular scintillating crystal design that uses silicon photomultipliers to measure physics signals from photons. The potential to develop particle identification methods using deep and traditional machine learning is explored. A contrastive machine learning technique was found to enable the separation of showering and 'punch-through' pions without explicit labels. A supervised particle identification method was then trained using the results, using both a graph neural network and a boosted decision tree to distinguish electron, showering hadron, and minimum-ionizing-particle-like events. The classifier achieved an area-under-the-receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.996 for both cases. A Shapley additive explanations analysis showed the boosted decision tree classifier matched expectations for each event type. The particle identification capability is then demonstrated on experimental data taken from the CERN Proton Synchrotron T9 beamline.

papers.title: Numerical Integration Instabilities in Likelihood Fits: Mechanisms and Remedies
papers.abstract: Numerical instabilities in the normalization of probability density functions can produce artificially lower negative log-likelihood (NLL) values than the true minimum of a likelihood fit, even when the resulting fit provides a poorer description of the data. Motivated by anomalously low NLL values found in non-converged fits associated with a recent CMS search for fully charmed tetraquark candidates, we use a pseudo-dataset generated from a likelihood model based on that analysis to investigate how numerical integration can yield unreliable normalization results, how these errors affect likelihood minimization, and how they can be addressed. We find that, even at fixed integration tolerance, the stopping decision of a numerical integrator can change with the fit parameters, introducing discontinuities in the normalization integrals that propagate to the likelihood surface. Such discontinuities can trap the minimizer at a numerical step and yield an artificially lower NLL. Tightening the integration tolerance mitigates these numerical discontinuities, while adaptive integration methods, such as Gauss--Kronrod quadrature, can also improve the numerical stability. A more severe failure occurs when the integration grid cannot adequately resolve a sharply localized contribution. In this case, the integrator may satisfy its estimated-error criterion despite substantially underestimating the normalization, allowing the minimizer to enter a region with an artificially low NLL. Tightening integration tolerances or using alternative adaptive integration methods does not necessarily resolve sharply localized contributions. We demonstrate that a suitable variable transformation can improve their numerical resolution, yielding more accurate normalization integrals and restoring fit convergence.

papers.title: Critical curves and throat degeneracy in black bounces
papers.abstract: Identical critical curves need not imply identical null-orbit dynamics. For a class of static spherical areal-radius deformations, we show that a surviving original photon sphere retains its critical impact parameter and orbital frequency, while its coordinate-time Lyapunov exponent is multiplied by the radial Jacobian. The logarithmic strong-deflection coefficient acquires the inverse factor. At a reflection-symmetric throat, stability factorizes into a derivative of the original optical potential and the throat curvature. More generally, an order-$m$ extremum of the original potential composed with an order-$q$ areal-radius minimum produces an optical degeneracy of order $p=mq$, with critical approach $|x|\propto|t|^{-2/(p-2)}$ and reflected strong deflection $Δφ\propto(b/b_{\rm c}-1)^{-(p-2)/(2p)}$ for $p>2$. For the Simpson--Visser family with mass $M$ and bounce parameter $a$, the critical impact parameter remains Schwarzschild-like for $a<3M$, although the instability varies with $a$. The merger at $a=3M$ is quartic, separating stable and unstable throat branches. These results isolate the null-orbit information preserved by a radial deformation from that encoded in its local geometry.

papers.title: Ab initio calculations of ${\barδ_\text{NS}}$ and extraction of ${V_{ud}}$ using effective field theory
papers.abstract: Radiative corrections limit the precision of $V_{ud}$ extractions from superallowed $β$ decays. In particular, the model dependence in the nuclear matrix elements (NMEs) is difficult to assess without a clear organizing principle, which is provided by effective field theory (EFT). We report substantial progress in this program based on ab initio nuclear calculations using the coupled cluster method. Benchmarking results against Quantum Monte Carlo calculations for light nuclei, we evaluate all two-body NMEs that enter the correction $\barδ_\text{NS}$ across 12 superallowed transitions relevant for $V_{ud}$, including an estimate of truncation and Hamiltonian uncertainties. We find that certain three-body NMEs at ${\mathcal O}(α^2)$ play an important role, due to a combination of large numerical prefactors and coherent scaling with $Z^2$. We develop a formalism to estimate such NMEs based on nuclear densities to complete the EFT evaluation of $\barδ_\text{NS}$, validating the corresponding two-body NMEs against ab initio calculations. We further identify the corrections in the traditional phase-space factor that are captured by the EFT and remove them consistently, which renders the individual transitions mutually consistent. Profiting from a recent calculation of ${\mathcal O}(α^2 Z)$ ultrasoft photons, we find that the scale uncertainty in the EFT is now negligible, while the remaining uncertainty is dominated by contact terms required to renormalize the magnetic Gamow-Teller NMEs. One combination of low-energy constants can be determined from a global fit to the superallowed data, but the second one proves strongly correlated with $V_{ud}$, necessitating additional input to resolve the nuclear-structure effects. We argue that such short-distance contributions currently imply an uncertainty in $V_{ud}$ at the level of $δV_{ud}\simeq 6\times 10^{-4}$.

papers.title: Decoding SO(5) Deconfined Multicriticality: Conformal Bootstrap and Fuzzy-Sphere Spectroscopy
papers.abstract: The nature of the deconfined quantum critical point (DQCP) remains unsettled: competing explanations invoke a real multicritical conformal field theory (CFT) or pseudocriticality governed by nearby complex fixed points. We use the conformal bootstrap and fuzzy-sphere regularization to compute $SO(5)$ CFT data and compare our results with large-scale quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) data to investigate these scenarios. Using mixed correlators of the lowest vector $φ$, singlet $s$, and traceless symmetric scalar $t$, we characterize the bootstrap cone whose tip lies remarkably close to the position indicated by large-scale QMC. We extract an extensive spectrum across $SO(5)$ irreducible representations, together with operator product expansion (OPE) coefficients. We study a fuzzy-sphere realization of the $SO(5)$ nonlinear sigma model with a level-1 Wess--Zumino--Witten term. Using the special conformal generators, we identify 52 conformal primaries in a system with \(N=10\) Landau orbitals, including 31 not previously classified as primaries in the earlier fuzzy-sphere study. Symmetry projection extends fuzzy-sphere exact diagonalization to $N=12$. The bootstrap spectrum and OPE coefficients show close agreement with fuzzy-sphere data, including 16 of the newly identified primaries in channels accessible to the mixed-correlator bootstrap. The lowest $SO(5)$ singlet scalar is relevant in the bootstrap and QMC results; its fuzzy-sphere data is $Δ_s=2.816$ at $N=12$ and decreases with system size. Our results suggest that the mixed-correlator bootstrap solution represents a unitary CFT with a relevant $SO(5)$ singlet scalar and is closely connected to the QMC and fuzzy-sphere data for the DQCP. The conformal bootstrap, fuzzy-sphere, and QMC together provide comprehensive evidence for an $SO(5)$ multicritical CFT and critical data to decode the phases in two-dimensional quantum magnets.

papers.title: Energy-flow bubbles at the Schwarzschild horizon and their Regge-pole clock
papers.abstract: For a circularly polarized plane wave scattered by a Schwarzschild black hole, the time-averaged energy flow on the side of the horizon facing the wave contains small, sealed recirculation cells. In the main family, pairs of zero circles are born on the axis and slide into the horizon in periodic frequency windows; at higher frequencies further cells appear off the axis. We map the cells for $κ=ωr_s/c\le10$ and show that each is the interference of a background integral with the leading photon-sphere Regge surface wave. A cell can die only at a zero of the circularly polarized field on the horizon, and all sixteen measured deaths are such zeros. A parabolic-cylinder analysis at the top of the potential barrier reduces this to a phase condition with a constant $π/4$ and no fitted parameter; recorded before the measurement, it predicted eight deaths in $6\leκ\le10$ to within 0.012 in $κ$. Electromagnetic duality makes the core of each main-family cell a circle of linear polarization; inside such a cell, flow lines lie on nested tori and close into torus knots of one chirality.

papers.title: Sharp fill-in inequalities and rigidity for spin initial data sets
papers.abstract: We prove sharp fill-in inequalities for compact spin initial data sets satisfying the dominant energy condition. The inequalities relate the spacetime mean curvature of the boundary to its hyperspherical radius and stable one-systole. Equality characterizes spacelike graphs of constant boundary height over round Euclidean balls and, in the systolic case after passing to the universal cover, over products of a round disk with Euclidean space. We also prove rigidity under comparison with strictly convex Euclidean domains, using normalized boundary metrics. The proofs use a modified Dirac operator with a chiral boundary condition.

papers.title: Bayesian Time-Varying Spectral Estimation for LISA with P-Splines
papers.abstract: We model the evolutionary spectrum of a slowly time-varying process by a linear combination of products of time- and frequency-dependent B-splines, placing a Gaussian tensor-product penalty prior on the coefficients. The posterior distribution is obtained by updating the prior using a Whittle-type likelihood approximation of the Wilson-Daubechies-Meyer time-frequency coefficients. Separate regularisation in time and frequency allows non-stationary spectral structure to be inferred. An adaptive coarse-grained likelihood reduces the computational cost while preserving fine resolution around sharp spectral features. We first validate the method using repeated simulations of a locally stationary process with known spectrum, showing lower reconstruction errors and narrower posterior intervals as the sample size increases. We then apply it to a year-long simulated LISA data set with stationary instrumental single link spectra, an evolving time-delay interferometry (TDI) response, and a modulated Galactic foreground. We compare a flexible total power spectral density (PSD) model with models incorporating progressively stronger physical information and examine both continuous and gapped observations. Allowing time variation substantially improves reconstruction relative to a stationary model, while incorporating physical information about the TDI response further improves recovery, particularly near its moving spectral features. The results illustrate the trade-off between spectral flexibility, physical assumptions, and posterior uncertainty in non-stationary LISA noise estimation.

papers.title: High-Statistics Study of Antiproton Annihilation at Rest on Argon in a LArTPC
papers.abstract: This paper reports a high-statistics study of antiproton--argon ($\bar{p}\text{--}\text{Ar}$) annihilation at rest in the J-PARC T98 experiment using a single-phase Liquid Argon Time Projection Chamber (LArTPC). A dataset comprising over $10^{5}$ annihilation events was acquired together with comprehensive calibration data. In parallel, a dedicated Geant4-based simulation framework was developed to model the secondary beam transport and detector response. Together, these experimental and computational resources provide a foundation for benchmarking hadronic interaction models and for future LArTPC-based antimatter searches, such as GRAMS. As an initial application of this framework, we compare the measured annihilation topologies, localized energy profiles, and spatial cluster multiplicities with predictions from three hadronic interaction generators: Fritiof, INCL++, and GiBUU. While all models reproduce the overall features of the total energy deposition, GiBUU provides the most consistent empirical description of localized energy deposition near the annihilation vertex and spatial cluster multiplicities at larger radii, reflecting the key roles of secondary nucleon knockout and in-medium pion absorption. These results provide a high-statistics experimental benchmark for modeling low-energy antiproton interactions in liquid argon.

papers.title: On Chen's Extended Action for $κ(R,T)$ Gravity: Gravity in a Polarizable Medium, Material Folds and a No-Bounce Theorem
papers.abstract: Chen's local adjoint action reproduces the field equations of $κ(R,T)$ from a local variational principle, and we show that it does physical work. In flat FLRW, Dirac reduction gives a Hamiltonian independent of $κ(T)$ on regular branches, where the coupling enters through a second-class matter constraint. The physical stress tensor is not generally conserved, but a dressed particle number is. An exact decomposition of the effective source motivates a polarizable-medium interpretation: $κ=0$ corresponds to total screening, the repulsive phase to overscreening, and a fold of the matter map to saturation. For linear coupling and dust, the expanding low-density branch has a past endpoint at the fold, where the volume is minimal and the density reaches $ρ_c/2$ at finite curvature. Dirac consistency rules out smooth Hamiltonian continuation through the fold. More generally, a flat-FLRW bounce is excluded for $κ>0$, positive density and $w>-1$. The linear dust model reproduces the effective Friedmann equation of loop quantum cosmology (LQC), but the two models obey different conservation laws. An effective pressure $-ρ^2/ρ_c$ restores the homogeneous LQC dynamics, and the fold density coincides with the signature-change threshold in the deformed-algebra approach to LQC. The reduced dust constraint admits an exactly solvable Koopman--von Neumann transport quantization and the adjoint field acts as a response variable, motivating an open-system interpretation.

papers.title: Study on net-proton number fluctuations in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{\textit{s}_{\text{NN}}}$ = 7.7-27 GeV with the SMASH model
papers.abstract: Higher-order cumulants ($C_n$) of the event-by-event net-proton number ($ΔN_{\mathrm{p}} = N_{\mathrm{p}} - N_{\bar{\mathrm{p}}}$) distributions are sensitive observables in the search for the QCD critical point. A reliable quantitative baseline for non-critical effects is essential for interpreting these observables. We calculate $C_2/\langle N_{\mathrm{p}} + N_{\bar{\mathrm{p}}}\rangle$, $C_3/C_1$, and $C_4/C_2$ in Au+Au collisions at collision energies $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 7.7$-$27$ GeV with the SMASH hadronic transport model. The collision-centrality, rapidity-window, and collision-energy dependences are reported. The cumulant ratios are predicted below the independent-Poisson baseline, with the suppression increasing toward more central collisions and larger rapidity windows. In 70-80% collisions, SMASH calculations lie above the STAR measurements for all three ratios, whereas in 0-5% collisions, the STAR $C_4/C_2$ value at 19.6 GeV lies below the SMASH reference with a pull of approximately $-2.7$. These results provide an independent non-critical hadronic baseline for assessing the model dependence of the observed data-model discrepancies.

papers.title: The PHAROS Spectral Library: Data Processing, Spectral Reconstruction, and Uncertainty Propagation
papers.abstract: We document the data reduction, reconstruction choices, and available uncertainty propagation underlying fifteen PHAROS stellar spectral energy distributions from 0.5 to 5000 nm. A catalogue timeline and a practical FITS guide introduce the available products, their column and extension conventions, and examples of reading, integration, and uncertainty display. Shared methods are presented once, including flux geometry, support-aware integration, X-ray likelihoods, the 2025 X/EUV luminosity relation, intrinsic Ly$α$ inference, airglow treatment, spectral junctions, and covariance-aware resampling. Target sections record the adopted observations and alternatives, including spatially separated binary components, unresolved system-level EUV measurements, direct EUVE constraints, optical stellar-twin transfer, and literature-anchored cases where new spectral inference is unsupported. The distinction between native measurement errors, conditional model intervals, empirical predictive scatter, and physical-method sensitivity is maintained. Signed measurements and nonnegative irradiation products are distinguished. Each target section concludes with the final nominal spectrum and its available uncertainty bounds on common axes. This library provides the detailed provenance and interpretation needed to accompany the catalogue paper and its machine-readable products.

papers.title: Multi-throat generalized Ellis--Bronnikov wormholes with asymptotic string-cloud behavior
papers.abstract: We study an ultrastatic, spherically symmetric family of traversable wormholes obtained by locally deforming a generalized Ellis--Bronnikov areal-radius profile in a spacetime with an asymptotic angular deficit. Depending on the deformation parameters, the same analytic family contains one, two, three, or four throats. The corresponding bifurcation curves are obtained in dimensionless form, and the resulting geometries are regular and asymptotically conical. We also reconstruct a source in General Relativity using a canonical scalar, a shift-symmetric phantom scalar, and a magnetic nonlinear electromagnetic field coupled to the canonical scalar. In the reference multi-throat geometry, the coupling removes a branch obstruction of an uncoupled single-valued nonlinear electrodynamics (NED); the same obstruction occurs whenever equal values of the magnetic invariant require different values of $\mathcal G_F$. For $\mathcal G(F)=F+λ\sqrt F$, the NED sector carries the leading asymptotic stress, which scales as $r^{-2}$ and approaches the string-cloud equation of state. The total stress tensor satisfies pointwise energy conditions in finite belly-centered regions of representative two- and four-throat solutions, while the throats violate the radial null energy condition (NEC) and the violation extends into integrable asymptotic tails. The Nandi--Zhang--Kumar covariant volume integral of $ρ+p_r$ is quadratic in the deformation amplitude; its zero is distinct from the bifurcation curves. Away from saddle-node boundaries, each throat supports a radially unstable background-metric light ring, and each intermediate belly supports a radially stable one, with an internally trapped null family in the double-throat case. These results place the topology, source reconstruction, integrated NEC content, and background-metric circular-orbit structure in a common parameter-space description.

papers.title: Directionality of low-energy electron recoils in the CYGNO experiment
papers.abstract: Electron-recoil directionality can help distinguish solar-neutrino interactions from backgrounds and, together with recoil-energy measurements and three-dimensional tracking, enable neutrino-energy spectroscopy. We study the reconstruction of the initial direction of low-energy electron recoils in the CYGNO optical time-projection chamber, focusing on the 50 L LIME prototype and its high-granularity scientific CMOS (sCMOS) readout. A dedicated algorithm identifies the interaction point from the asymmetry of the track light distribution and estimates the recoil direction from the early portion of the ionization trail, before multiple scattering erases most of the directional information. The method is characterized with a detailed Monte Carlo simulation of electron recoils and detector response. Samples spanning 15 keV to 70 keV are used to optimize the algorithm parameters by minimizing the width of the reconstructed-minus-true projected-angle distribution. The projected angular response is modeled by two Gaussian components that account for its dependence on track inclination. The narrower component, associated with favorable projections approximately parallel to the Gas Electron Multiplier (GEM) plane, has a width that improves from about $20^\circ$ near 20 keV to about $12^\circ$ at 60 keV. We also quantify the fraction of events in the correctly reconstructed angular core and discuss the dominant limitations of a camera-only two-dimensional measurement.

papers.title: Electric-magnetic asymmetry of exact dyonic Euler-Heisenberg black holes: duality-blind shadows and magnetically controlled horizons
papers.abstract: Maxwell theory is invariant under electric-magnetic rotations, and the Reissner-Nordström black hole depends on its charges only through the sum of their squares. The Euler-Heisenberg vacuum-polarization terms break this symmetry, and an exact dyonic Einstein-Euler-Heisenberg black hole was found recently. We ask which properties remember the breaking. Outside the photon sphere, almost none do. The metric function is even under charge exchange through first order in the coupling, the first odd term appears at second order and falls off as the tenth inverse power of the radius, and the shifts it causes in the shadow, the Lyapunov exponent, and the innermost stable circular orbit stay at a few parts per million. The core behaves differently. Any magnetic charge drives the metric function to negative infinity at the center and so forces a horizon, while an electric configuration lighter than its field energy can be horizonless. Whether an extremal limit exists is decided by one function of the charges, the maximum of the derivative of the mass function, whose critical curve reaches the origin along the electric axis and meets the magnetic axis at a closed-form value. Two independent integrations confirm every number, and the shadow is tested against the Event Horizon Telescope image of Sagittarius A*.

papers.title: Variational and geometric time-dependent density-functional theory of electronic systems
papers.abstract: A central problem in time-dependent density-functional theory (TDDFT) is to construct a time-dependent many-electron wave function that reproduces a prescribed time-dependent electron density. This problem admits a natural geometric interpretation, which in turn leads to at least two distinct formulations of TDDFT. The first is the usual variational formulation of TDDFT, in which the density constraint is enforced with a real-valued local potential. The second is geometric TDDFT, introduced in recent works, in which the same density constraint is enforced with an imaginary local potential, or equivalently with a Hermitian nonlocal potential. In this work, we develop this unified viewpoint for continuous electronic systems and systematically compare the two formulations. We formulate the corresponding time-dependent Kohn-Sham schemes and derive a number of exact conditions for geometric TDDFT, including conditions associated with causality, time-reversal symmetry, uniform-coordinate scaling, translational invariance, energy and momentum equations of motion, one-electron self-interaction, and the adiabatic limit. The paper also contains a mathematical section where we provide a fully rigorous justification of some parts of the text. We particularly discuss the mathematical properties of two operators underlying the two formulations of TDDFT and establish sufficient conditions for their invertibility. We explain the functional-analytic subtleties underlying the geometric interpretation of TDDFT and the two formulations of TDDFT. This unified perspective clarifies the mathematical and conceptual relation between variational and geometric TDDFT and provides a foundation for the development of approximations within geometric TDDFT.

papers.title: Microcausality Bounds on Dispersion Laws
papers.abstract: Microcausality holds in any state, including those that spontaneously break Lorentz invariance, and requires the poles (and other singularities) of the retarded Green's function to satisfy $\mathrm{Im}\,ω\le |\mathrm{Im}\,k|$ throughout the complex plane. Building on the work of Heller, Serantes, Spaliński and Withers, we study its consequences for dispersion relations that are linear at small $k$, like Goldstone bosons, assuming tree-level, non-dissipative dynamics. We show that microcausality is equivalent to requiring that $k \pm ω(k)$ be typically real functions. This yields two-sided bounds on all higher-order coefficients of $ω(k)$ in units of its radius of convergence $R$, the scale at which the linear Goldstone description breaks down. The optimal constraints are characterised by an infinite hierarchy of Toeplitz determinants. We derive analogous bounds on $ω^2(k)$, whose radius of convergence $\tilde R$ marks the scale at which new states must appear. The bounds shrink to zero as the sound speed $c_s$ approaches 1: for a fixed higher-derivative correction, both $R$ and $\tilde R$ become parametrically smaller than naive dimensional analysis suggests. In particular, in the EFT of Inflation all higher-derivative quadratic operators must vanish as $c_s \to 1$. We test the bounds in several models: a $U(1)$ superfluid, light in a dielectric medium, photon propagation in a strong magnetic field, colour-flavour-locked quark matter, and a homogeneous solid. Finally, we extend the bounds to gapped modes.

papers.title: On the equivalence of three extended Calogero--Bogoyavlenskii--Schiff models to the classical CBS equation
papers.abstract: We examine the three extended Calogero--Bogoyavlenskii--Schiff (CBS) models introduced by Wazwaz, Alhejaili, and El-Tantawy [Eur.\ Phys.\ J.\ Plus \textbf{141}, 1218 (2026)]. Explicit invertible point transformations map the first model, and generically the second, to the classical CBS equation. The third model is generically equivalent to CBS with an additional spectator coordinate absent from the differential operator. We identify the exceptional parameter regimes and explain the reported exponential dispersion relations through these transformations. These equivalences show that the proposed models do not, in the generic parameter regimes, introduce new point-inequivalent CBS equations or genuine four-variable differential coupling.

papers.title: Quantum chaos from time-dependent CFT states at large central charge
papers.abstract: We provide a first study of the behavior of four probes on heavy, time-dependent background states of conformal field theories at large central charge. Employing the monodromy method and including subleading corrections to the identity block, we compute the correlation function of two light and two middle-heavy operators on such a heavy background, by switching on a small interaction between the light and middle-heavy sectors. Summing the discontinuity contributions and analytically continuing from Euclidean to Lorentzian signature, we show that the out-of-time-ordered correlator (OTOC) exhibits maximal chaos, that is, the Lyapunov exponent saturates the MSS bound.

papers.title: LAMOST III Low-resolution Spectroscopic Survey: Overview and Target Selection
papers.abstract: We present an overview of the LAMOST III Low-resolution Spectroscopic Survey (LRS), including its scientific goals, target selection strategy, and current observing status. Targets in the main survey are selected via weighted random sampling, using the inverse local density in the Hertzsprung-Russell (HR) diagram and in the G-magnitude distribution, with additional enhancement in selected regions of the HR diagram. The main survey is complemented by 35 dedicated add-on catalogs (including very metal-poor star candidates, halo stars, hot/young stars, wide binaries, extragalactic sources and so on) and a time-domain program providing multi-epoch spectroscopy of binaries and other peculiar systems. LAMOST III LRS is designed to map the structure and evolution of the Galactic disk, reconstruct the assembly and early chemical-enrichment history of the Galactic halo, improve stellar-parameter calibration, and characterize rare and variable objects. By June 2025, the LAMOST III LRS had obtained 1.53 million low-resolution spectra from 658 plates, corresponding to 1,264,052 unique sources. Relative to LAMOST I+II, the current sample is enriched in O/B stars, subgiants, main-sequence turn-off stars, metal-poor stars, and other previously underrepresented populations. In particular, the fractions of metal-poor and very metal-poor stars increase from 3.8% and 0.4% in LAMOST I+II to 9.0% and 1.1% in LAMOST III LRS, respectively, demonstrating the improved efficiency of the revised target-selection strategy for Galactic archaeology and stellar astrophysics.

papers.title: The fate of hidden symmetries under magnetic Harrison transformations
papers.abstract: Solution-generating transformations construct new geometries from known seeds, raising the question of whether and to what extent the resulting solutions inherit the hidden symmetries underlying the seeds' integrability and separability. We have established universal perturbative inheritance laws for CKTs and massless scalar separability directly at the level of magnetic Harrison transformations, encompassing both magnetization of Carter-type seeds and demagnetization of conformal Carter-type seeds. In both magnetized Kerr and demagnetized Kerr-Bertotti-Robinson, this perturbative inheritance coexists with the loss of exact Carter-type separability, while seed-connected conformal Killing-Yano structures are already obstructed at the same perturbative order. These results reveal a hierarchy in the perturbative survival of hidden symmetries and provide a framework for investigating their inheritance in more general theoretical settings and under other solution-generating transformations.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal K-Shape: Reconstructing inhomogeneous condensate profiles on the lattice
papers.abstract: Spatially modulated chiral condensates can affect the phase structure of dense QCD effective models. Understanding such order requires characterizing its real-space structure as well as detecting a modulation. Spatial two-point correlators retain the ensemble-averaged power spectrum but discard relative Fourier phases, leaving the configuration shapes undetermined in general. We propose the Spatiotemporal K-Shape method to extract representative shapes from lattice Monte Carlo ensembles without assuming a functional form. The method extends K-Shape clustering to periodic lattice fields, aligning configurations modulo translations and, optionally, a global sign or phase before extracting cluster centroids. Comparisons across clusterings assess whether one representative shape suffices. Controlled tests recover distinct profiles with identical correlators and separate mixtures of different shapes. Applied to the $(1+1)$-dimensional Gross-Neveu model with $N_f=8$, the method extracts non-sinusoidal profiles with two sign changes at two chemical potentials and separates multiple shape families at a third, where a single centroid is insufficient. Including the discrete chiral sign symmetry in the alignment can fold domain-length fluctuations into an asymmetric centroid without implying a preferred ensemble asymmetry. The method thus complements correlator diagnostics with representative real-space shapes and information on their diversity. The application to the Gross-Neveu model provides a testing ground for configuration-based studies of inhomogeneous order relevant to the QCD phase diagram.

papers.title: Doubly strange tetraquark as a $KK^*$ virtual state: quark-model study with harmonic traps
papers.abstract: We extract hadron--hadron scattering information from quark-level interactions using an artificial harmonic trap and a four-quark basis that includes both meson--meson and compact diquark--antidiquark configurations. Combining the Busch--Englert--Rzażewski--Wilkens formula with the effective range expansion (ERE), we determine phase shifts, scattering lengths, effective ranges, and pole positions from the trapped spectrum. We control uncertainties from basis truncation, finite trap frequencies, truncation of ERE, and quark-model parameters. The extracted $DD^*$ and $BB^*$ binding energies agree with direct calculations, providing benchmarks. For the doubly strange $T_{ss}$ with $I(J^P)=0(1^+)$, we predict a $KK^*$ virtual-state pole about 30--35~MeV below threshold in the stable-$K^*$ approximation. Both the AL1 model and its modified version that better reproduces the measured $T_{cc}^+$ binding energy yield this result. This finding differs from earlier predictions of a bound state and motivates searches for the $T_{ss}$ at facilities such as the High Intensity heavy Ion Accelerator Facility (HIAF). This framework could be extended to other hadron-hadron channels to extract scattering observables and pole positions.

papers.title: Quantum-correlation of neutral charmed mesons at BESIII
papers.abstract: Quantum-correlated $D\bar D$ pairs give direct access to the strong-phase differences between $D^0$ and $\bar D^0$ decays, which are essential inputs to the CKM angle $γ$ and charm mixing. The BESIII experiment has accumulated the largest data sample at the $ψ(3770)$ resonance, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $20.3\,\text{fb}^{-1}$. The neutral $D\bar D$ pairs produced at $ψ(3770)$ are in a $C$-odd state. We report new and improved measurements of the strong-phase differences in $D\rightarrow K_{S,L}π^+π^-$, $D\rightarrow K^+K^-π^+π^-$, $D\rightarrow K^-π^+π^+π^-$ and $D\rightarrow K^-π^+π^0$ decays, alongside a measurement of the $CP$-even fraction in $D\rightarrow K^+K^-π^+π^-$. Furthermore, we present a novel method that studies the $D\bar D$ quantum correlations using data collected at centre-of-mass energies from $4.13$ to $4.23\,$GeV, where the $D\bar D$ pairs are produced in $C$-even or $C$-odd states, according to the number of accompanying photons. This gives the first observation of $C$-even $D\bar D$ pairs and a new measurement of the strong-phase difference in $D\rightarrow K^-π^+$ decays.

papers.title: Negative and Positive Saddle-Selection Ambiguities in the HTEE
papers.abstract: The holographic timelike entanglement entropy (HTEE), computed via complexified extremal surfaces, suffers from a saddle-selection ambiguity: for sufficiently small time intervals (\(Δt\to0\)), both a vacuum-connected and a vacuum-disconnected complex extremal surface contribute, and the minimal-real-part criterion and the vacuum-reduction criterion can favor different saddles. We study this ambiguity in strongly coupled field theories whose dual geometries are hyperscaling-violating Lifshitz backgrounds, in which conformal symmetry and Lorentz invariance are broken by the Lifshitz exponent and the hyperscaling-violation parameter. Working in \(2+1\)- and \(3+1\)-dimensional dual field theories, we derive general expressions for the HTEE in the vacuum-connected and vacuum-disconnected saddles, \(s_{v.c.}\) and \(s_{v.d.}\), respectively, and compare their real parts. We find that the two criteria agree everywhere except at the first accidental zero. The ambiguity appears in two distinct forms. In the \emph{negative} family, \(\operatorname{Re}(s_{v.c.})=0\) and \(\operatorname{Re}(s_{v.d.})<0\), whereas in the \emph{positive} family, \(\operatorname{Re}(s_{v.c.})>0\) and \(\operatorname{Re}(s_{v.d.})=0\). The latter shows that the ambiguity survives even in the conformal \(3+1\)-dimensional case. It therefore seems that the saddle-selection ambiguity is a generic feature of the complexified-geometry prescription.

papers.title: Schwarzschild scattering from CFT
papers.abstract: We show that retarded CFT correlators on $\mathbb{R}\times \mathbb{S}^2$ in a state described by the small black hole in AdS$_4$ can be used to derive asymptotically flat Schwarzschild partial-wave S-matrix elements, including its spectrum of quasinormal modes. This is achieved by identifying a class of operators for which the dual bulk fields behave as plane waves near the AdS boundary for sufficiently high frequencies. For such operators there is a simple analytic relation between CFT correlators and reflection coefficients which behaves gracefully in the flat space limit, $L\to \infty$. These include spin-1, spin-2, and conformally coupled scalars. We provide a simple toy model that captures how dissipative QNMs can appear for short times inside Hermitian systems, closely resembling the small black hole in AdS.

papers.title: Emptiness formation in quantum fluids: a hydrodynamic solution
papers.abstract: We develop an auxiliary-kernel method for constructing the hydrodynamic instantons that govern macroscopic emptiness formation in one-dimensional Galilean quantum fluids. The key step is to represent the equation of state by an auxiliary integral kernel inspired by the Bethe ansatz. For equations of state admitting such a representation, we reduce the imaginary-time hydrodynamic problem to a single integral equation. Its solution determines the full density and current profiles, the vacuum boundary, and the leading emptiness rate. Notably, the construction does not require microscopic integrability. For the Lieb--Liniger gas, we derive the previously conjectured integral equation for the leading rate and use a known elliptic solution to obtain explicit expressions for the rate and vacuum boundary. Direct hydrodynamic numerics support the predicted boundary. We also recover known instanton solutions for a family of polytropic fluids.

papers.title: Gaia as a 0.1 arcsec point-source survey across the sky: dynamical scene reconstruction from one-dimensional scans
papers.abstract: Gaia has observed every detected source on the sky 50 to 100 times, each time through a window of about 1 by 2 arcseconds at a different scan angle. The resulting one-dimensional flux profiles to be released in Gaia DR4 encode the two-dimensional arrangement of nearby point sources at ~0.1 arcsecond resolution. Repeated observations also constrain their relative motion. We present a method to model the scene with a mixture of moving point sources. Complementing Gaia DPAC's source-environment reconstruction, our approach focuses on close, blended companions and models their relative motion. We first fit each window with a few point sources and obtain their along-scan positions. We then triangulate these positions from different scan angles to identify candidate sources on the sky. A joint forward model of all windows measures positions, fluxes, relative proper motions, and parallax differences, even for blended components. In simulations, we recover companions at separations smaller than the instrumental profile width. For a moving companion at ~75 mas separation with a flux ratio of ~0.2, we obtain a separation precision of ~0.1 mas and a relative proper-motion precision of ~0.1 mas/yr per component, even in a scene contaminated by a third source. These precisions assume a known instrumental profile and independent Gaussian noise. We also recover differential parallax for a chance-aligned source. Modeling nearby contaminants prevents significant biases. With a Gaia-like instrumental profile, sampling and scan law, we show a sensitivity of ~5 mag in contrast at separations of 50-150 mas, and we discuss its dependence on the color term of Gaia's line-spread function. The method could extend the census of close companions and provide relative astrometry, and so dynamical information, along short orbital arcs. External measurements could also guide retrospective searches in Gaia's windows.

papers.title: Muon and Tau Anomalies and $Δα_{had}^{(5)} (M_Z^2)$ in the Standard Model
papers.abstract: I review the present status of the Standard Model (SM) determination of the muon anomaly by emphasizing the estimate of the lowest hadronic vacuum polarization contributions using recent $e^+e^-$ data on $2π$ and $3π$ and the inclusive ratio $R^{ee}$ of total cross-sections compiled by PDG to which we add the QCD continuum including HO PT QCD up to $α_s^5$, quark mass $m_q^2$ up to $α_s^3$, $m_s^4$ up to $α_s^2$ and QCD condensates. Adding the $e^+e^-\to π^0γ+ ηγ$ contributions to the CMD3 data, one obtains\,: $a_μ\vert^{hvp}_{lo}=(7094\pm 37)\times 10^{-11}$. Combining this LO result with the HO estimate of the hadronic, QED and EW contributions, one obtains\,: $Δa_μ^{sm} \equiv (a_μ^{exp}-a_μ^{sm})= (86\pm 38_{th}\pm 14.5_{exp})\times 10^{-11} $. The average of the recent estimates quoted in Table\,3 [$\oplus$ attempt to fit all $\,e^+e^-$ data] gives\,: $Δa_μ^{sm} = (84.9[90.0]\pm 21.3_{th}\pm 14.5_{exp})\times 10^{-11}$\,. These results agree with the precise BMW20 lattice one and still suggest a window for new physics beyond the SM of $(2.1\sim 3.5)\,σ$. Besides some future projects for improving the $e^+e^-$ data, the MUonE for extracting directly $a_μ^{tot}\vert^{hvp}_{lo}$ and J-PARC (E34) for an independent measurement of $a_μ$, it is important to improve the Lattice results shown in Fig.\,9 which (at first sight) disagree each others despite the large errors and may question the reliability of the {\it averages of different averages} used in the White Paper (WP25) Our analysis is completed by updating the estimate of the hadronic contribution to the tau anomaly\,: $a_τ\vert^{hvp}_{lo}=(3516\pm 25)\times 10^{-9}$ and to $α(M_Z)\,: \,Δα_{had}^{(5)} (M_Z^2)= (2770.7\pm 4.5)\times 10^{-5}. $

papers.title: Local field shifts and the Gribov-Zwanziger horizon functional
papers.abstract: We study a Maggiore-Schaden-like re-centering of the Gribov-Zwanziger action using a smooth compactly supported profile. At fixed background and finite cutoff, under the stated coercivity and contour hypotheses, this transformation preserves the original horizon functional with no residual dependence on the profile. The extension to gauge-field integration requires additional domination assumptions. Near a self-adjoint first Gribov horizon, the response depends on both the lowest Faddeev-Popov eigenvalue and its source weight. We extend this visibility analysis to non-self-adjoint compressions, separating source darkness from truncation-induced shielding, and recall continuum transverse $SU(2)$ examples. Transporting the composite insertion preserves the regulated Gaussian and resolvent structure. A separate free-space tree-level check reproduces the auxiliary-mass denominator of the RGZ propagator, without determining condensate dynamics

papers.title: Pairing connections between localized nuclear regions: Orbital reweighting and thermal quenching
papers.abstract: The nucleon localization function (NLF) characterizes nuclear spatial structure; the nonlocal anomalous density (pairing tensor) describes coherent pair amplitude between two points. Global pairing measures leave connections between distinct spatial regions unresolved. We determine how selective orbital participation strengthens pairing connections between localized regions during overall pairing loss, and why heating attenuates the connection while preserving its pattern. Axial Hartree-Fock plus BCS calculations combine NLF with the pairing tensor in shape-constrained 20Ne (distinct localization lobes) and octupole-deformed 144Ba (reflection-asymmetric background). Complete signed orbital sums separate anomalous-weight and spatial-kernel changes at fixed pairing strength and cutoff. Contraction along a constrained 20Ne branch preserves identifiable end lobes while reducing total anomalous norm and increasing the absolute opposite-end integral. Coupled spectrum and gap changes favor a mixed 1d5/2/2s1/2 component and deplete anomalous participation of a predominantly 1p1/2 component. Increased positive strength and weaker destructive interference overcome the net opposing spatial-kernel response; this balance survives mesh refinement. Heating at the reference quadrupole constraint yields compensating thermal and quasiparticle-energy factors, so similar gap reductions produce nearly common attenuation. In 144Ba, octupole deformation and normal-localization modulation persist after anomalous sources vanish. Regional enhancement depends on how selective anomalous participation changes the complete signed orbital sum, including spatial feedback. Nearly proportional participation changes preserve the pattern when kernels remain stable, distinguishing stronger absolute connections from larger normalized fractions on an identifiable localization background.

papers.title: A Bound on Wormhole Probing Time from Holographic Multi-Entropy
papers.abstract: Bipartite entanglement entropy eventually saturates and therefore cannot track the continued growth of an eternal wormhole. Recently, it was shown that genuine tripartite multi-entropy can probe wormhole growth even after bipartite entanglement entropies have saturated. This naturally raises the question: can increasing the number of parties extend the probing time indefinitely? Adopting the multiway maximin prescription and assuming that its selected representatives are regular spacetime-stationary networks, we prove that the answer is no for nonrotating BTZ black holes. We establish a common finite upper bound on the probing time for every fixed finite boundary partition, independent of the number, sizes, and arrangement of its parties. For any network on any Cauchy slice, there exists a comparison network that assigns the entire central region containing the wormhole interior to a single party. A network longer than this comparison network cannot minimize length on that slice. The central length required by a stationary network connecting the two boundaries grows with time, whereas the central length of the comparison network remains uniformly bounded. At sufficiently late times, such a network therefore cannot minimize length on any Cauchy slice containing it and is excluded from the maximin prescription. Consequently, beyond this bound, no network selected by maximin enters the black-hole interior.

papers.title: Canonical metrics on punctured spheres, II: compactified moduli spaces of black holes
papers.abstract: Let $g_{\mathfrak{p}_{\ell}}$ denote the canonical scalar-flat metric on $S^n\setminus \mathfrak{p}_{\ell}$ introduced in Part~I, which for $n=3$ corresponds to the Brill--Lindquist initial data for $\ell$ black holes, and let $η\in H_{\ell}$ be its associated mass matrix. In this paper, we investigate the asymptotic behavior of the metrics and the mass matrix $η$ as subsets of punctures collide. Such collisions cause every mass to diverge; if a cluster $A$ of black holes collapses at a relative scale $t$, the mass matrix satisfies $η=E(A)\ln(1/t)+O(1)$, diverging along an explicit ray $E(A)\in H_{\ell}$. For nested families of clusters, this degeneracy structure naturally organizes into a space of rooted trees. Subtracting the divergence gives a renormalized mass matrix which extends smoothly to every stratum of the Axelrod--Singer compactified moduli space $\overline{M}{}^{\,\mathrm{AS}}_\ell= \overline C_{\ell-1}(\mathbb{R}^n)/\mathrm O(n)$ and splits naturally into one mass matrix per vertex of the bubble tree. Geometrically, at each vertex carrying punctures the suitably rescaled metrics converge to a complete scalar-flat metric with the nodes filled in, adjacent such pieces being joined by Schwarzschild necks, and the renormalized matrix acting as its mass data. For $n=3$, the necks contain minimal spheres, which are common apparent horizons of the merging holes. At vertices bearing two holes, we determine on which side of the limiting horizon each node lies, and we formulate as a conjecture the resulting criterion for a neck to be a component of the outermost horizon. We also compare the mass lower bound of Part~I with the Riemannian Penrose inequality. Because the mass matrix is invariant under rotations of the bubbles, it lives on a Deligne--Mumford-type quotient of the compactification.

papers.title: On the Spontaneous symmetry breaking of Conformal Gravity to Weyl and Einstein Gravities
papers.abstract: Does the special-conformal connection remain an auxiliary field when a spontaneously broken conformal gauge theory is promoted to a fully dynamical Yang-Mills-Higgs theory, and under what conditions does its elimination yield Weyl gravity? We address these questions within an $\mathrm{SO}(2,4)$ gauge-theoretic formulation of gravity. Revisiting the gravitational sector selected by spontaneous symmetry breaking through an adjoint $15$-plet, we retain the special-conformal connection as an independent field and demonstrate that, on a source-free projected branch, its algebraic equation of motion determines it in terms of the Schouten tensor. Eliminating this connection yields the four-dimensional Weyl-squared action, up to the Euler density, without imposing the Schouten relation as an additional geometrical constraint. We then extend the analysis to the standard local Yang-Mills-Higgs theory and show that the special-conformal connection remains auxiliary, owing to the structure of the invariant bilinear form of $\mathfrak{so}(2,4)$, which prevents the appearance of an independent kinetic operator. The additional gauge and scalar sectors can modify its algebraic solution, so the exact Weyl reduction is restricted to the source-free branch. We further investigate the linearised spectrum of the reduced Weyl theory around de Sitter spacetime, identifying massless and partially massless spin-2 branches, with the latter occurring at $m_{\mathrm{PM}}^2=2Λ/3$. Finally, we discuss the subsequent symmetry breaking induced by an antisymmetric scalar $6$-plet and its role in connecting the Weyl-gravity phase to Einstein gravity.

papers.title: Holographic Einstein rings of a covariant quantum corrected AdS black hole
papers.abstract: We investigate holographic Einstein rings in a covariant quantum corrected Schwarzschild--AdS$_4$ spacetime using a massless scalar probe. At fixed horizon radius $r_h$, the deformation parameter $ζ$ leaves the metric mass parameter, coordinate surface gravity, and photon sphere radius unchanged, while increasing the photon potential maximum and the asymptotic lapse coefficient $A=1+ζ^2$. The critical coordinate impact parameter approaches $A^{-1/2}$ for large black holes, whereas the corresponding incidence angle in the normalized boundary frame approaches $π/2$. Ray tracing and local WKB barrier data recover the same geometric scale. Quasinormal spectra computed with AdS boundary conditions provide a comparison at finite multipole number. These results separate the finite radius effect of the deformation from the change in boundary time normalization.

papers.title: Skyrmions coupled to the sigma meson
papers.abstract: We propose a geometric coupling of the Skyrme model of nuclei to the scalar--isoscalar sigma meson by identifying the sigma field with the radial length of the chiral four-vector while preserving the topological protection of the baryon number. Restricting to the $B=1$ hedgehog ansatz, an asymptotic analysis of the field equations shows that the in-vacuum sigma mass $m_σ$ is replaced inside the nucleon by an effective in-medium mass $m_{σ,{\rm eff}} = 2m_π$. Full numerical integration via a double-shooting method and parameter optimization demonstrate that including the sigma meson leads to a remarkable improvement in the description of nucleon observables and to a pion decay constant very close to its physical value.

papers.title: Generalized transverse-momentum-dependent parton distributions of a photon and orbital angular momentum
papers.abstract: The coefficients of generalized transverse-momentum-dependent distributions (GTMDs) that encode the canonical fermion orbital angular momentum and spin--orbit correlation do not contribute to the direct transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) and generalized-parton-distribution (GPD) projections. We present, to our knowledge, the first explicit calculation of the leading-twist, time-even, chiral-even fermion GTMDs of an on-shell real photon at zero skewness and order $α$. The coefficients $\mathcal{F}_A$ and $\mathcal{G}_A$, which multiply the $k_\perp\timesΔ_\perp$ structure, yield the fermion orbital angular momentum $\ell_z^f$ and spin--orbit correlation $\mathcal{C}_z^f$. For photon helicity $+1$, both are obtained in closed form in the leading fermion--antifermion sector and obey $\mathcal{C}_z^f=-\ell_z^f/2$ for a common transverse regulator independent of $x$, because the channel with the active fermion's spin anti-aligned with its orbital motion carries three times the integrated weight of the aligned channel. The projections reproduce the known photon TMDs and leading-logarithmic photon-to-fermion kernels, and energy-momentum-tensor overlaps reproduce the known one-loop photon gravitational form factors $F_1$, $F_2$, and $F_3$. Our result provides an analytic benchmark for fermionic orbital and spin--orbit structure in the real photon.

papers.title: A Paired Monte Carlo Intensity-Ratio Method for Incorporating Detector Resolution in Amplitude Analysis
papers.abstract: Finite detector resolution can bias resonance parameters and fit fractions extracted from amplitude analyses. We present the paired Monte Carlo intensity-ratio method for incorporating resolution effects into amplitude analysis. The method uses ratios of reference intensities evaluated at paired truth-level and reconstructed kinematics to reweight the Monte Carlo normalization and approximately account for detector resolution. A resampling study of simulated $D^+\to K^+π^+π^-π^0$ decays shows that the method substantially reduces resolution-induced shifts in fitted resonance widths. Likelihood evaluation uses intensity calculations and normalization sums, avoiding a response convolution at each data event.

papers.title: Certifying quantum generative models beyond the Fisher trace
papers.abstract: Whether a trained quantum generative model has learned its target is usually decided by a diagnostic validated on a labeled benchmark, and such a diagnostic can pass that validation by recovering how the benchmark was built. We analyze Fisher-trace and kernel-based certification of the real-amplitude quantum circuit Born machine in noiseless statevector simulation. For real-amplitude circuits built from half-angle rotations, the classical Fisher information equals the quantum Fisher information almost everywhere, so its trace equals the parameter count and carries no information about fit quality. The Fisher eigenvalue rank counts the live nodes of the amplitude tree: it coincides with the label on a sparse benchmark and is uninformative on a full-support one. The pooled Wasserstein and maximum-mean-discrepancy scores move with optimizer convergence and with the scoring convention. For two bitstring defect families on which both metrics have closed forms, we compute the tolerance-mismatch window in which the discrepancy rejects generators that the transport threshold admits; it opens only at certification-grade tolerances and closes as the qubit number grows. On the Hamming cost we prove a sharp tolerance ratio above which the discrepancy vote is redundant, and we obtain the exact worst-parity minimax value over all unit-diagonal positive-semidefinite kernels, which is exponentially small in the qubit number. In a numerical campaign at the tolerances a near-term experiment can resolve, the discrepancy vote changed no verdict at a thousand shots or more. The false-pass guarantee does not extend to device noise.

papers.title: From Quasinormal Mode Poles to Branch Cuts at Finite $N$
papers.abstract: In the strict large-$N$ limit, holographic thermal retarded correlators are typigcally meromorphic, with their late-time behavior determined by isolated quasinormal mode (QNM) poles. We show that the first bulk-loop correction, of order $1/N^2$, qualitatively changes this structure. In a scalar theory on the planar AdS$_5$ black brane, a one-loop bulk diagram generates poles at sums of two QNM frequencies at fixed loop momentum $q$; integration over the continuous momentum turns these QNM-pair poles into branch cuts. At vanishing external spatial momentum, for pairs built from QNM branches with opposite real parts, the leading light-cone contributions cancel at large momentum, and the residual QNM-pair frequency scales as $q^{-1/3}$. Consequently, an infinite family of cuts accumulates at zero frequency, while all tree-level QNM poles remain at finite nonzero frequencies. The first finite-$N$ correction therefore closes the gap set by the classical QNM spectrum. Competition between the decreasing QNM-pair damping and thermal Boltzmann suppression produces a moving saddle and a finite-$N$ contribution $G(t)\sim N^{-2}t^αe^{-Ct^{3/4}},\, C>0,$ which decays more slowly than the leading classical QNM contribution. Thus the large-$N$ expansion is nonuniform at late times, and bulk quantum fluctuations generate a distinct late-time regime beyond the classical QNM decay.

papers.title: Two-scale system: compactified ambient metrics and Scri/Spi/Ti
papers.abstract: We show that certain geometric constructions, including the Fefferman-Graham ambient metric, Brinkmann spaces, and ultrastatic vacuum spacetimes, admit natural conformal compactifications and can be unified within a single framework arising naturally from conformal geometry. The framework is based on a two-scale system comprising two weight-one conformal scalars satisfying almost-Einstein equations and certain regularity conditions. As a particular instance of this unifying framework, we obtain a new ambient construction for Spi and Ti, the extended spatial and temporal infinities of Ricci-flat spacetimes. A remarkable feature of this construction is that Spi/Ti and the null infinity of the corresponding spacetimes are naturally realised as a boundary face and the corner of the two-scale ambient space, respectively. We also demonstrate how the two-scale system can serve as a background ambient geometry for studying the asymptotic behaviour of (gauge) fields at spatial, temporal, and null infinity.

background.title: Slow and rapid mixing in $\mathbb{Z}_2$ hyperlattice gauge theory
background.abstract: The Ising model under Glauber dynamics on the torus is known to exhibit a phase transition in its mixing time. The mixing is exponentially slow when $β>β_c$ and logarithmically fast when $β<β_c$. In this paper, we generalize the slow-mixing result to $\mathbb{Z}_2$ hyperlattice gauge theory when $β$ is large enough. This is a higher-dimensional analogue of the Ising model, with spins on $k$-cells. Specifically, on the torus of any dimension $m \ge k+2$, we prove explicit exponential lower bounds on the mixing time of Glauber dynamics when $β$ is sufficiently large. More precisely, we prove that the result holds for a broader class of dynamics, allowing more than one $k$-cell to change its value at each step of the algorithm. Finally, we show that there are distinct slow and rapid mixing regimes, as for sufficiently small $β$ the Dobrushin condition is satisfied for Glauber dynamics under the heat-bath rule, which implies logarithmic mixing.

background.title: Polarization of Fast Radio Bursts due to Propagation in Magnetized Plasma
background.abstract: Polarization measurements of radio transients, particularly their frequency dependence, shed light on the magnetic environments of these sources. We extend the analytical solution of radiative transfer of the polarization properties of such transients to both a cold magnetized plasmas beyond the high-frequency approximation and a relativistic plasma with synchrotron emission. The Faraday mixing coefficients are enhanced makes Stokes parameters $Q$, $U$, and $V$ to exhibit a more rapid and complex frequency-dependent evolution. A relativistic plasma medium can also generate both Faraday roataion and conversion with a smaller magnetic field. The relativistic plasma is investigated as a persistent radio source (PRS) associated with FRB, and it is found that, although the observed PRS luminosity can be accounted for, an FRB can propagate out only under certain special parameter conditions. We apply the model to fit the polarization profile of GPM J1839$-$10 and revisit some FRBs. All sources with Faraday conversion require that the environment's magnetic field not exceed 100~G. The magnetic field of FRB 20180301A and GPM J1839$-$10 are almost perpendicular to the light of sight for at least some times.

background.title: Spectral Moments of the Projected Hubbard Configuration Graph: Connectivity, Exchange, and Virtual Doublons
background.abstract: At strong on-site repulsion, the lowest band of $n$ lattice fermions is the spectrum of the hopping projected onto configurations without double occupancy, $H_\infty=P_0H_tP_0$. We study its moments, for few fermions in the square-lattice Hubbard model and, where the arguments allow, on any finite graph. (1) For spin-independent Hermitian hopping (no on-site terms) on any $N\geq2$-site graph, $μ_2=\frac{n(N-n)}{N(N-1)}\sum_{i\neq j}|t_{ij}|^2$, for any spin composition. (2) On any finite graph, $μ_4$ is exactly linear in the same-spin pair count, as four hops permute particles by at most a transposition or 3-cycle; for uniform hopping on a simple graph with $N\geq4$ the slope is $α(N,n)=-8C_4(N-n)(8N-11n-2)/[N(N-1)(N-2)(N-3)]$, fixed by the number $C_4$ of 4-cycles. (3) At large finite $U$, the second-order Schrieffer-Wolff correction is Hilbert-Schmidt orthogonal to $H_\infty$ on every triangle-free graph, so the band variance has no $1/U$ term; its $U^{-2}$ coefficient, an exact trace checked by exact diagonalization, is negative at the low fillings computed. (4) Under a Peierls flux, the exchange slope $α(N,2,Φ)=-\frac{64}{N-1}\cosΦ_\square$ ($L\times L$ tori, $L=3$ or $L\geq5$) carries the ordinary charge-$e$ harmonic, while the doublon (bound-pair) hopping acquires a doubled phase, $t_de^{2iA_{ij}}$: the second-order single-doublon Hamiltonian is exactly $π$-periodic ($h/2e$) under a boundary twist, and the exact two-electron U-band follows numerically, up to $O((2λ)^L/U^{L-1})$. Result (1), the permutation bound, the orthogonality in (3) and the doubled phase are machine-checked in Lean 4. Repulsive binding and the pair charge $2e$ are known; new are the exact moment structure and the derivation of the doubled phase. We make no claim about many-pair phase stiffness, off-diagonal long-range order or superconductivity.

background.title: XRISM/Xtend detection of solar wind charge exchange induced by multiple coronal mass ejections in 2024 August
background.abstract: Solar wind charge exchange (SWCX) emission is often a major component of the soft X-ray background, but it also provides a remote diagnostic of the composition and ionization state of solar wind plasma. We present an analysis of a SWCX event observed with XRISM/Xtend during 2024 August 9-13. The event occurred during intense solar activity with multiple flares, including an X1.3-class solar flare, and associated coronal mass ejections (CMEs). We found a clear enhancement in the 0.3-3.0 keV count rate that occurred nearly simultaneously with an increase in the solar wind proton flux measured by ACE. We fitted the spectrum during the enhancement period with a set of Gaussian emission lines. In addition to the commonly detected C, N, and O lines, we detected Ne, Mg, Si, and Fe lines at $>15σ$ significance. We extracted two characteristic periods within the enhanced interval based on the CME arrival timeline. The O$_{\rm VIII}$/Si$_{\rm XIII}$ line ratio changed significantly between the two periods, suggesting contributions from multiple CME components. We then applied the AtomDB charge exchange model with a multi-temperature setup. The estimated ionization temperatures for Ne, Mg, Si, and Fe increased with the peak soft X-ray flux of the associated solar flares. This trend suggests that coronal heating becomes more efficient for more intense flares. Meanwhile, the ionization temperatures were lower than typical flare electron temperatures, implying that CME plasma may have been released into interplanetary space under non-equilibrium ionization conditions. We also found an indication of an inverse-FIP pattern, with reduced relative abundances of Si and S. These results demonstrate that XRISM/Xtend can diagnose the coronal plasma through SWCX emission, including heavy ions such as Ne, Mg, and Si, which are difficult to measure with current in-situ instruments (e.g., ACE satellite).

background.title: Matrix Star-Triangle Relations
background.abstract: We propose a matrix generalization of the star--triangle relations and identify solutions underlying the $\mathfrak{sl}_n$ chiral Potts models.

background.title: Character variety of the punctured sphere and the determinantal variety
background.abstract: We show that the SL(2;C) character variety of the n-punctured sphere is described via the determinantal variety defined by an n x n symmetric matrix of rank at most 4 whose entries are the traces of simple closed curves on the surface. This result generalizes the Fricke-Klein-Vogt relations to arbitrary n, and we determine the structure of the kernel of the associated matrix.

background.title: Metric perturbations in Einstein-Hilbert gravity: An alternative perturbative formulation
background.abstract: We derive the ordinary gauge-fixed quadratic operators of the four-dimensional Einstein--Hilbert action in exponential and inverse-metric-density variables on an arbitrary reference background. With a single nonlinear background-harmonic gauge transported through the exact field map, the density operator is the trace-reversed Lichnerowicz operator, while the exponential operator contains an additional algebraic Ricci-curvature term. This difference arises from the nonlinear transformation of the background tadpole and vanishes on Ricci-flat backgrounds; a cosmological-constant check gives the corresponding cancellation at Einstein saddles. The construction retains the exact determinant contribution and specifies the associated Faddeev--Popov operator. At the first interacting order on a flat background, we show that the two gauge-fixed cubic actions differ by a term proportional to the free field equation, and independently evaluate the same nonzero three-point coefficient in both variables, with its normalization matched to the Einstein-gravity interaction. An exact Schwarzschild configuration satisfies the same background-harmonic gauge and is stationary under unrestricted exterior variations of the gauge-fixed action. Its density and exponential reconstructions are checked together with the bulk and boundary terms; a separate radial variation illustrates the loss of an equation after imposing a restricted ansatz. These results provide an explicit comparison of established field coordinates at the classical and tree levels; quantum loop calculations additionally require a common measure, regulator and source prescription.

background.title: A Five-Dimensional Geometric Formulation of Geophysical Fluid Dynamics
background.abstract: We apply a geometric formulation of Newtonian dynamics to inviscid compressible geophysical flow, with gravity and the effects of rotating or moving coordinates incorporated in the metric tensor. This construction relies on the introduction of an auxiliary fifth coordinate, which allows mass and momentum transport, internal energy, and pressure work to be combined into a single mass--momentum tensor. The covariant divergence of this tensor leads to the continuity equation for mass density, the three momentum equations, and the thermodynamic equation, with the system closed by an equation of state. A time-independent metric also yields conservation of total energy. We recover familiar forms of the equations and illustrate the construction in rotating spherical and terrain-following coordinates. The thin-shell and spherical-geopotential approximations, with constant effective gravity, simplify the metric while retaining vertical gravity and the traditional Coriolis terms. Emphasis is placed on the connection between the geometric structure of the formulation and the equations commonly used in atmospheric dynamics.

background.title: Gauge aspects of teleparallel gravity and Noether's second theorem
background.abstract: We examine the gauge structure of the Teleparallel Equivalent of General Relativity (TEGR) from the perspective of Noether's second theorem. We show that diffeomorphisms and local Lorentz transformations are the gauge symmetries of TEGR, as these are the only variational symmetries that give rise to Noether identities. We then discuss the distinct roles of these two symmetries and their implications for the gauge-theoretic interpretation of gravity. Finally, we discuss consequences of these observations for the role of translations in gauge theories of gravity and the coupling of matter in TEGR. In particular, we demonstrate that the matter coupling prescription is uniquely determined and coincides with that of general relativity, including in the case of spinor fields.

background.title: Confinement--Higgs Complementarity Viewed through Relative Quantum Reference Frames
background.abstract: We formulate confinement--Higgs complementarity in terms of the relative orientation between two independently constructed quantum reference frames (QRFs): one derived from the gauge field and the other from the scalar field. Exact continuum and lattice identities give a relational interpretation of the scalar--color observables used in recent gauge-fixing-free $SU(2)$ simulations. In particular, we provide a QRF interpretation of the additional gauge-invariant nonlocal separation line obtained from the Cho--Duan--Ge (CDG) reduction reported in lattice simulations of the radially fixed fundamental $SU(2)$ gauge--scalar model. We explain why such a candidate nonlocal boundary is compatible with Fradkin--Shenker continuity and Osterwalder--Seiler analyticity for the appropriate class of local gauge-invariant observables. Separately, we show that a Wilson-rooted control observable admits an exact results at zero plaquette coupling and that it does not cause such a nonlocal separation line.

background.title: Magnetic Power in Binaries: From Coalescing Binary Neutron Stars to Close-in Exoplanetary Systems
background.abstract: A binary system containing two magnetic components ("stars") can be modeled as a circuit powered by the orbital motion, with the magnetic field lines linking the two stars serving as wires. When the total resistance in the binary components is small -- as found in many astrophysical systems such as binary neutron stars and extra-solar hot-Jupiter or super-Earth systems -- the connected field lines are twisted and open up in a quasi-cyclic manner, leading to quasi-periodic energy dissipation and flares. We derive analytic expressions for the average and episodic magnetic powers from such systems, providing a quantitative description on how the powers depend on the magnetic orientations of the two stars. The power can be much larger than in the case where one of the stars has a negligible magnetic field. It may manifest as pre-merger quasi-cyclic flares in coalescing neutron-star binaries and as orbit-regulated radio emissions in exoplanetary systems.

background.title: Cartan geometry and the Hamiltonian analysis of gravitational actions in terms of forms
background.abstract: The purpose of the paper is to review the Hamiltonian formulation for several actions related to general relativity that can be written in terms of differential forms. As we will show the powerful ideas of Cartan geometry can be used to simplify the Hamiltonian analysis and arrive at a coherent and comprehensive geometrical understanding of it.

background.title: All edges lead to Rome: analyzing Late Antiquity regime shifts using coin hoard data
background.abstract: Complex network analysis and other statistical techniques can be fruitfully applied to historical data to understand dynamics that brought the territory under study to a certain state. In this paper we use the FLAME database to understand when a drastic change of trade regime occurred in the Italian peninsula by looking at mint-hoard links that are evidence of a physical connection between them. By using changepoint analysis to pinpoint precise dates in the time series of these links, and then historical as well as network data to establish the sequence of network collapse, we find that the demise of the Western Roman Empire started at the beginning of the 5th century AD, yielding a more precise sequence of how and when it reached Italia.

background.title: A proof of Nakamura's conjecture
background.abstract: We prove Nakamura's conjecture on the relation between the 2D Toda model and solutions of the Ernst equation, using the Pfaffian solutions obtained in our previous work arXiv:2610.27420.

background.title: Peak state transfer in trees and the cost of distance
background.abstract: There is peak state transfer between vertices $u$ and $v$ in a graph $G$ if there exists a time $t$ for which $|(\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm i t M})_{u,v}|$ saturates the triangle inequality imposed by its spectral decomposition and $M$ is either the adjacency or Laplacian matrix. We show that peak state transfer at distance $d$ requires $\frac{d^3}{24}(1 + o(1))$ edges in the adjacency case, $Ω(d^2)$ edges in the Laplacian case, and that the leading coefficient in the former is tight. We find a family of graphs with Laplacian peak state transfer at distance $d$ and $Θ(d^5)$ edges, showing that peak state transfer is achievable in a polynomial graph size. In contrast, Laplacian perfect state transfer costs at least $Ω(2^{d/2})$ edges when the distance partition of vertices around one vertex is almost equitable. Finally, we show that Laplacian peak state transfer in trees requires $Ω(d!)$ edges, and we characterize all trees of diameter $\leq 4$ admitting Laplacian peak state transfer, thus answering a pair of questions posed by Coutinho, Guo, and Schmeits.

background.title: Deformation Quantization of Coisotropic A-branes
background.abstract: Motivated by the Gukov--Witten proposal that the endomorphism algebra of a coisotropic A-brane should be described by a deformation quantization of its transverse holomorphic symplectic geometry at the perturbative level, we study deformation quantization on transverse holomorphic symplectic manifolds $(M,Ω)$. Extending the approach of Nest--Tsygan to this setting, we show that, under an admissibility condition, equivalence classes of deformation quantizations are in bijection with \[ \hbar H^2\bigl(\operatorname{F}_1Ω^\bullet(M,\mathbb C),d\bigr) [[\hbar]], \] where $\operatorname{F}_1Ω^\bullet(M,\mathbb C)$ is the differential ideal generated by transverse $(1,0)$-forms. We further illustrate this framework through examples arising from mapping tori, $T$-duality, and coisotropic lifts in cotangent bundles. These examples clarify the roles of admissibility and the transverse Atiyah class, as well as the distinction between deformation quantizations and global star products. Finally, for a coisotropic A-brane $M$ induced from a transverse complex manifold $Q$, we use transverse jets and the Fock representation to construct a perturbative level action $End(M)\curvearrowright Hom(M,Q)$ under suitable compatibility assumptions, providing a geometric realization of the brane quantization philosophy.

background.title: The Lukashian Calendar: A universal calendar mechanism using variable-duration years and days for any human colony or settlement
background.abstract: Existing calendars, in particular the Gregorian calendar, have a complex structure which requires constant adjustment in the form of leap days and leap seconds in order to remain synchronized to the position of a planet in the Solar System. In addition, mean solar days can deviate up to 16 minutes from true solar days on Earth. On other planets, this discrepancy can be far greater: on Mars, it can be up to 51 minutes. Numerous Martian proposals ranging from Aitken (1936) to Gangale (1986) to Silin (2025) mimic the Gregorian calendar and do not address these issues. Moreover, many do not include a system for telling the time of day, or stretch the second beyond the standard SI second.
